segments.text: A Harbor Board member asks Morgan what the preparation agent actually did for the proposed
session.
Morgan could hand over the entire trace.
That would reveal source notes and internal deliberation the board member did not request.
Morgan could write a polished story from memory.
That would be hard to check.
We need a smaller packet, enough to show the boundary, the work, the hold, and the
human decision without dragging every underlying record into the room.
Chapter 21's scoped proof loop has six fields.
Audience, scope, window, exclusions, export, and ledger.
For the Harbor Board reader, scope is one session option paper case across one course
planning window.
Include the permitted job, evidence status summary, handoff result, the staffing hold,
Morgan's paper disposition, and the still unapproved print request.
Exclude raw source text, prompts, private reasoning, unrelated people, and any actual
records.
The packet records what is known and what is withheld.
It does not certify agent quality or imply a session happened.
The workbook calls for capability boundaries, scoped trace references, approval
decisions, cost authority summary, export metadata, and reviewer notes.
Use course references and a course timestamp label, not a real log.
Morgan reviews the proposed proof packet before any sharing.
If a field cannot be safely summarized, mark it withheld with a reason.
Redaction is a decision, not a blur laid over a screenshot.
Here, the export is only a classroom outline.
Nothing is sent.
The same team then hears an idea, a tiny phone tool that helps volunteer
coordinators compare workshop options.
The temptation is to build it because it fits the Harbor story.
Chapter 22 asks for a foundry test first.
Demand, monetization, builder fit, build velocity, differentiation,
release readiness, and approval gates.
The workbook proposes a weighted score out of 100.
A score is useful only when each field has attributable evidence.
Our class has no real market research, pay or interview, or release review.
Those fields stay unscored.
A number without evidence would turn an idea into false proof.
Write the smallest safe next test.
Morgan could ask for permission to research public demand and
clarify who would pay.
Even that is a proposed plan, not a provider call or outreach.
No repository, tester invite, user data collection, price, store listing,
or public claim follows from this lesson.
A phone can display the packet and a hold status, but it cannot wave the gate.
The valuable outcome may be a decision to shelve the idea.
That saves time a rushed build would consume.
Pause.
What would you leave out of the board packet even if it helped tell a better story?
Draft a client safe proof packet outline for the harbor planning case.
State audience, scope, window, inclusions, exclusions, export review,
and ledger fields.
Redact the course trace in words rather than pasting it.
Then make a foundry test for the volunteer coordinator tool.
Mark each evidence field observed, missing, or unscored.
Name a payer question, a tiny proposed test, the human gate, and a stop condition.
Use a fictional or approved example.
Do not use private operational data, contact a person, create a repo, or generate a public claim.
Save revision 12 as a draft.
Harbor now has a way to explain its held work and a way to examine a new idea
without pretending either is ready to ship.
The operating file keeps the missing evidence visible.
That is what makes the next human decision honest.
